decisions.reason: The source establishes a main-board JST connection to the LEDs but does not change the daughterboard's LED count, part, supply voltage, or board form.
The source's confirmation that the standalone USB LDO is on the main board is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
A main-board connector to the LED chain does not change the charge-status display method or the separate power-board charge-LED interface.
The source confirms that the main board has a connector to the power board but supplies no new connector partition, type, pinout, or matching policy.
The source places power management outside the main board but does not change the boost converter, enable control, powered loads, or 5V routing.
The mention of pull-ups and series resistors on the main board is consistent with the candidate's existing state and provides no new values or topology.
The source's button, reset, touch, and BOOT-button requirements are already represented by the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE.
The USB-C programming-port role established by the source is already represented by the candidate's same-message MODIFY.
The source describes the contents of the existing main board and confirms functional separation without changing the board count or board inventory.
The main-board connector inventory does not change the power board's battery-connector placement, orientation, spacing, or mechanical accessibility.
The source notes the INA219's 3.3V connection and excludes power management from the main board, but it does not change DCDC1 voltage, rating, or load role.
The source's main-board inventory and exclusion of power management do not change the battery NTC connector, function, or controller.
